policy: Publishing any component release (collab-cli-vX.Y.Z bus CLI, or ext-vX.Y.Z VS Code extension .vsix) requires an explicit, committed sign-off from BOTH the WIN and LINUX planes for that exact version. Each component's release workflow fails closed (blocks its publish job) unless both planes have recorded agreed:true. This encodes the operator directive: publishing shall occur only after bidirectional WIN<->LINUX agreement. Neither plane may unilaterally ship a shared release. collab-cli sign-offs live under the top-level `releases` map (backward-compatible); other components live under `components.<name>.releases`.

0.13.0.summary: net send --stream (persistent-connection, multi-frame streaming): ONE TCP connection carries --count N seq'd bus-msg@1 frames (seq S..S+N-1; --seq sets S) + an optional terminal DONE(S+N-1) via --done, with a single bulk flush (BusWire.WriteFrame gains a flush parameter) instead of the per-frame connect+flush of the single-frame send. Preserves the bus-msg@1 framing + strict per-(sessionId,senderId) seq order; ADDITIVE + back-compat (no --stream = the single-frame path byte-for-byte unchanged). Lifts a source from ~87 frames/s (one process per frame) to the transport/disk ceiling (~784k small frames/s; ~3.0 GB/s to the wire; ~1.46 GB/s to NVMe, disk-bound). Payload is --message/--message-file or --frame-bytes B filler. Plus experiments/throughput-to-disk/ (tpd), the .NET harness used to find the plateau. LbaBus.csproj 0.12.0 -> 0.13.0 + CHANGELOG. #214.

0.11.0.summary: net beacon interface/broadcast control (#155): `--bind <ip>` pins the SOURCE NIC so beacons egress a chosen interface (e.g. the host-only mesh 192.168.56.x) instead of the OS default/NAT route; SO_BROADCAST is enabled for a subnet-directed target (a --hosts entry ending in .255, e.g. 192.168.56.255) or an explicit --broadcast, not only the literal 255.255.255.255; per-host beacon sends are now loss-safe (a per-host send error skips only that peer for the round, matching the advisory/loss-safe ADR-0004 contract already applied to DNS-resolve misses); a startup `[net] beacon bind=.. udp=.. broadcast=.. hosts=..` diagnostic makes the egress choice visible. Answers WIN's mesh finding #2 (beacon egressed the NAT NIC -> 255.255.255.255, not the intended host-only mesh). LbaBus.csproj 0.10.0 -> 0.11.0 + CHANGELOG.

LINUX.note: Authored the net beacon enhancement (#155, merged to main at 0cc94b1) answering WIN's mesh finding #2: on the actors `lbabus net beacon` egressed the NAT NIC -> 255.255.255.255 (limited broadcast), not the host-only mesh 192.168.56.x. Added --bind <ip> (source-NIC pin, mirrors net listen --bind; invalid IP fails closed), directed/explicit broadcast (SO_BROADCAST for a .255 target or --broadcast, not only literal 255.255.255.255), loss-safe per-host sends (a per-host send error skips only that peer -- the unreachable-directed-broadcast case -- matching the ADR-0004 advisory contract), and a startup egress diagnostic. dotnet build clean; manually proven 5 ways (--bind loopback binds+sends; --broadcast + .255 set the flag; unreachable 192.168.56.255 skipped while 127.0.0.1 delivers; invalid --bind exits 1; default 255.255.255.255 unchanged). #155 CI all green incl. the Windows lbabus-verify image build (8m, no infra flake). Existing mesh-actor.{sh,ps1} pass unicast peer IPs (broadcast stays off) + discard beacon stderr, so unaffected. LINUX agrees to publish collab-cli-v0.11.0.

WIN.note: Validated on the WIN plane (Windows, dotnet 8.0, Release build of linux/collab-cli-0.11.0 @ 4faf539). dotnet build clean: 0 warnings / 0 errors, LbaBus.csproj Version 0.11.0, CHANGELOG [0.11.0] entry present. Reviewed the CmdBeacon diff (48a4cd3) end-to-end and it correctly answers my mesh finding #2: --bind creates `new UdpClient(new IPEndPoint(bindIp, 0))` to pin the SOURCE NIC (so beacons egress the chosen host-only 192.168.56.x instead of the NAT default route); broadcast now = explicit --broadcast OR a target ending in .255 (SO_BROADCAST enabled), not only literal 255.255.255.255; resolve+send moved into ONE per-host try so a per-host error skips only that peer (loss-safe, ADR-0004); and the `[net] beacon bind=.. udp=.. broadcast=.. hosts=..` startup diagnostic makes egress visible. Ran the built binary on Windows: (1) `--bind 999.1.1.1` -> `--bind: invalid IP` + exit 1 (fails closed); (2) `--bind 127.0.0.1 --hosts 127.0.0.1` -> diag `bind=127.0.0.1 broadcast=False`, unicast delivered; (3) `--hosts 192.168.56.255` -> diag `bind=auto broadcast=True` (SO_BROADCAST for the directed subnet). Confirmed this closes the mesh loop I proved this session: real lbabus net beacon --hosts (host-only unicast) -> my read-only mesh-monitor.mjs received the real bus-msg@1 envelopes on 7421 (capture.ps1 proved the pktmon L2 side); with 0.11.0 the actors can now `--bind 192.168.56.<n>` to guarantee host-only egress regardless of the NAT default route. Existing mesh-actor.{sh,ps1} pass unicast peer IPs (broadcast stays off), so they're unaffected. WIN agrees to publish collab-cli-v0.11.0.
